rules.sentence: About 2.4% of the world population is affected by peripheral nerve disorders; the prevalence increases to 8% in older populations.[3]
Diabetic neuropathy occurs in approximately half of individuals with chronic type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
Globally, leprosy remains a common cause of peripheral neuropathy, with the highest prevalence in Southeast Asia.
The most common genetic sensorimotor polyneuropathy is Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, specifically, type 1a.
The most common mononeuropathy is carpal tunnel syndrome.
